claims.claim: The spectral slope and natural radius counts agree exactly with the pinned finite native-camera geometry
The aligned C2, odd natural and even natural coefficient profiles have the stated exact divisibility formulas and periods
Every supported native-camera profile has zero coefficient mean over one exact spectral period
The aligned C2, odd natural and even natural complex camera factors are defined by the explicit source formulas
All supported explicit camera factors have the stated universal floor, including its alternate closed form, and are nonzero on s = 1/2 + i t
The pinned finite native operator has an exact free integer-coefficient realization with literal scalar coefficient extraction
Every aligned C2 finite coefficient equals the exact periodic profile on its emitted window and vanishes outside

Every natural odd-camera finite coefficient equals its periodic profile on the full emitted window; every natural even-camera coefficient equals its profile before the final antipodal point and differs there by exactly one unit
On Re(s) > 1, every supported periodic camera-profile Dirichlet series is summable and equals its explicit camera factor times the common positive-index series, equivalently Mathlib's riemannZeta
For every supported camera, the literal center-bracket series is absolutely summable on Re(s) > -1 and its finite cutoffs converge pointwise to the infinite bracket characteristic
For each supported camera, the center-bracket series converges normally on Re(s) > -1, finite characteristics converge locally uniformly, and the infinite characteristic is holomorphic there

Complex evaluation of the free finite stencil gives the exact C2, odd and even profile Dirichlet prefixes, including the even antipodal correction, and those prefixes converge to their profile series on Re(s) > 1
On Re(s) > 1, the infinite bracket characteristic equals the unified profile series and its explicit factor times Mathlib's riemannZeta, yielding the initial cross-factor identity
All supported factors are entire and the cross-factor identity extends by the analytic identity principle to the full connected half-plane Re(s) > -1
Camera 3 defines a holomorphic native scalar on -1 < Re(s) < 1; every supported camera factors through it there and all supported camera characteristics have the same zero set on the native line

A cutoff of M aligned center blocks approximates each supported native-line bracket characteristic with an explicit O(M^(-3/2)) remainder, and the stable finite-camera cross residual has the same rate

The centered exponent derivative series is termwise valid and summable on the native line; both the complex-exponent derivative and the actual t derivative of the M-block characteristic have an explicit O(M^(-3/2) log M) tail
For every fixed order k, Cauchy estimates on a dynamic complex disc prove both the complex-exponent and actual native-line t-derivative cutoff rates O(M^(-3/2) log(M)^k)

Every supported camera factor is a local analytic unit at native-line points, so all supported camera characteristics have the same analytic order of vanishing there; every finite positive zero order transfers exactly between cameras

Finite holomorphic zero order is preserved under restriction to the native real line; Complex.normSq doubles that real analytic order, and multiplication by a nonzero real-analytic weight preserves the doubled order

The five limiting sectors 3, 4, 5, 7 and mixed have the exact source factors, including the binary defect factor in the aggregated rank-two mode 4 and its product with A_3 in the mixed mode; their positive real-analytic weights and nonnegative real-analytic energies satisfy E_j(t) = Q_j(t) normSq(Z_nat), share the native scalar zero set, and turn a camera zero of finite complex order m into exact real energy order 2m

Every positive-definite finite Gram matrix has a canonical positive inverse square root R satisfying R^2 = G^-1 and R G R = I; whitening preserves Hermitianity and positive semidefiniteness, the variance equals R (J - H G^-1 H) R and is positive whenever the moment block is positive, and the period-420 cameras 2 through 7 instantiate the canonical self-adjoint whitened operators

Its entries are exactly ell, ell log ell and ell (1 + log(ell)^2). Hence the documented period-420 six-camera moment block and canonical variance are positive semidefinite.

For every finite camera family, the continuous step density D(x) M0 D(x) is pointwise positive semidefinite and Bochner-integrable, its vector measure is positive on every measurable set and has total mass G, and positive-definite G normalizes it by congruence with G^-1/2 to a POVM of total mass I. Every periodic sequence valued in a real normed vector space has Cesaro mean equal to its one-period average. If scalar weights are antitone, tend to zero, and have divergent total mass, the same conclusion holds for normalized weighted means by a Dirichlet-Abel argument with uniformly bounded centered prefix sums.

For every supported finite camera family and every weight satisfying the explicit Dirichlet-Abel and asymptotically-linear mass hypotheses, the genuine pairwise cutoff covariance up to min(ell_i,ell_j) M converges uniformly in finite-matrix norm to the periodic camera Gram matrix. In particular, cameras 2 through 7 converge to the exact documented six-camera Gram matrix under those hypotheses.

For every fixed nonreal z, the concrete logarithmic resolvent weight is positive, tends to zero, is eventually antitone, has mass A_M(z) asymptotic to M/log(M+1)^2, and satisfies A_(L M)(z)/A_M(z) -> L for every fixed positive natural L. Therefore the genuine resolvent-weighted finite-camera covariance converges in matrix norm to the periodic Gram matrix, with cameras 2 through 7 converging to the exact sixCameraGram.

The exact finite return metric G_E = I + P^*P makes every endpoint map E satisfying P E = B and E^*E + B^*B = I an isometry, so the return-metric source-probe covariance cancels exactly to the direct camera-resolvent covariance. The literal finite camera matrix includes every seed and corrected even endpoint coefficient; its normalized covariance differs from the shifted periodic core only by a uniformly finite resolvent tail, which vanishes. Consequently every compatible cutoff-indexed finite colligation family converges in matrix norm to the complexified periodic Gram, and cameras 2 through 7 converge to the exact sixCameraGram.

For every real spectral multiplier and every compatible finite return-metric colligation, the functional cross covariance cancels exactly to the direct observable-resolvent covariance and equals the complete literal finite coefficient sum. This specializes to every real polynomial evaluated at log(n+1) minus the finite resolvent-weighted logarithmic mean; the constant polynomial recovers the order-zero covariance. Any limit proved for the literal functional coefficient sums transfers automatically to both the direct matrix product and the return-metric colligation family.

The algebraic functional-moment target is kernel checked in every natural degree. The polynomial family P_0=1 and P_k=(1+X)^k-k P_(k-1) is defined once in Polynomial R, and every P_k is proved monic with natural degree exactly k. For every finite camera family the general matrix has entries G_ij P_k(log(min(ell_i,ell_j))) and is Hermitian and self-adjoint. Degrees zero through eight are proved equal to the previously checked concrete moment matrices, and cameras 2 through 7 admit one exact literal self-adjoint matrix for every degree. This claim is algebraic and does not assert scalar or covariance convergence beyond degree eight.

The first countable all-bases camera layer is kernel checked. Camera labels b >= 2 form the countable index, each pairwise periodic mean is defined over the least common multiple of its slopes and is proved invariant under every larger positive common period, and every finite principal restriction is exactly the previously checked finite periodic Gram matrix. The exceptional duplicated slope four has exact C2/C4 periodic-mean block [[3/2,5/2],[5/2,11/2]], determinant 2 and positive definiteness. A level/residue sum-of-squares identity proves every finite principal all-bases Gram matrix strictly positive definite and the induced Gram form strictly positive on every nonzero Finsupp vector. This first claim stops at the algebraic Finsupp layer; the canonical completion is covered by the following claim.

The canonical all-bases camera Hilbert completion is kernel checked without choosing an external camera weight. The strictly positive Finsupp Gram form satisfies all real bilinear inner-product laws and induces the intrinsic norm with norm square g_infinity(u,u). Mathlib's canonical completion is explicitly complete; its linear-isometric embedding preserves the Gram inner product and norm and has dense range. Canonical single-camera vectors have inner products exactly G_bc. The subspaces supported on labels at most B are monotone, their isometric inclusions are compatible as B increases, every finitely supported vector belongs to one such level, and the union of all finite-level images is dense in the completion. This claim does not construct an all-bases POVM, a Cauchy family or a Weyl inverse.

The canonical Kolmogorov realization of the all-bases periodic profile-mean kernel m_bc is kernel checked. Every finite principal restriction is identified with the finite periodic mean matrix and is positive semidefinite. Its bilinear Finsupp form satisfies the real pre-inner-product laws and is nonnegative; Mathlib's completion separates its seminorm-zero vectors and produces a complete Hilbert space K_0. The canonical vectors r_b satisfy inner(r_b,r_c)=m_bc exactly, every embedded finitely supported vector is their finite linear combination, and their algebraic span is dense. This claim deliberately does not realize the slope-minimum factor, construct the L2 Naimark isometry, promote the finite POVM to all bases, or construct a Cauchy/Weyl family.

The explicit all-bases Naimark isometry is kernel checked. Lebesgue measure restricted to the positive half-line and the intervals (0,ell_b] realize the slope-minimum factor exactly. The L2 vectors 1_(0,ell_b] r_b have almost-everywhere indicator representatives and inner products equal to the full all-bases Gram kernel G_bc. Their finite linear-combination map preserves the intrinsic Gram inner product and norm on CameraFinsupp. It extends along the dense canonical embedding to a norm- and inner-product-preserving real linear isometry from CameraHilbert into L2((0,infinity),K_0), sending every canonical camera vector to its documented indicator vector. This claim does not yet construct logarithmic multiplication, a projection-valued measure, the compressed Cauchy family or the unbounded Weyl inverse.

The logarithmic spectral multiplier on the explicit all-bases Naimark space is kernel checked through its densely defined symmetric closable stage. The documented coordinate y(x)=1+log(x) is measurable, and multiplication by y is bundled as a LinearPMap on the exact maximal domain of L2 vectors for which yf remains in L2. Its almost-everywhere action is literal. Every explicit camera vector 1_(0,ell_b]r_b and every finite camera-core combination lies in the domain, using the checked singular-endpoint integral of y squared. Multiplication by the bounded positive regularizer (1+abs(y))^(-1) has trivial kernel, symmetric dense range contained in the maximal domain, proving that domain dense. The logarithmic multiplier is formally self-adjoint in the symmetry sense, hence closable, and its canonical graph closure is closed. This claim does not assert that the original multiplier is closed or equal to its Hilbert-space adjoint; it does not yet construct a projection-valued measure, compressed Cauchy family or Weyl inverse.

The natural maximal logarithmic multiplication operator on the all-bases Naimark space is kernel checked as a self-adjoint closed LinearPMap. Composing its everywhere-positive regularizer R=(1+abs(y))^(-1) with logarithmic multiplication gives the bounded real transfer multiplier yR. Testing the Hilbert-space adjoint identity on regularized vectors proves (yR)g=R(Y-adjoint g) for every adjoint-domain vector; pointwise cancellation of R gives the literal almost-everywhere adjoint action Y-adjoint g=yg and places g in the natural maximal domain. Symmetry supplies the reverse operator inclusion, so the adjoint domain equals the maximal multiplication domain, Y-adjoint=Y, and Y is self-adjoint and closed. Its canonical graph closure equals Y itself. This claim does not yet construct explicit spectral projections, the compressed Cauchy family or the unbounded Weyl inverse.

The canonical realified all-bases compressed Cauchy family is kernel checked for every nonreal spectral parameter lambda. The real and imaginary scalar parts of (lambda-y)^(-1), with y=1+log(x), are measurable and satisfy the exact two-component inverse identities, the reciprocal-denominator squared-modulus identity, conjugation symmetry and the standard resolvent-scale component bounds by abs(Im lambda)^(-1). They define bounded self-adjoint real multiplication operators on the Naimark L2 space with literal almost-everywhere action and the corresponding operator-norm estimates. Compression by the explicit Naimark isometry gives the real and imaginary components corresponding to V-adjoint (lambda-Y)^(-1) V on CameraHilbert. Both compressed components are self-adjoint, obey the same norm estimates and conjugation laws, and the imaginary component has strict negative quadratic form in the upper half-plane and strict positive form in the lower half-plane. Consequently it is injective and has dense range for every nonreal lambda. Because CameraHilbert is currently real, this claim packages the Cauchy family as its canonical real/imaginary operator pair; it does not construct a separate complex Hilbert-space realization, an explicit projection-valued measure or the unbounded Weyl inverse.

The complete all-bases Cauchy family is kernel checked on the underlying real Hilbert space of the canonical complexification WithLp 2 (CameraHilbert x CameraHilbert). For symmetric real and imaginary components A and B, the standard real block sends (x,y) to (Ax-By,Bx+Ay), its skew quadratic form is the sum of the two B quadratic forms, and its adjoint is the conjugate block A-iB. Applying these facts to the compressed Cauchy components transfers the strict upper- and lower-half-plane sign to every nonzero doubled vector. Hence the full block is injective. Conjugation of the spectral parameter identifies its adjoint with another injective Cauchy block, so the Hilbert-space orthogonal-range identity proves that the full block has dense range. This is a real block realization; no independent complex scalar action is asserted.

For every nonreal spectral parameter, the inverse of the complete all-bases Cauchy block is kernel checked as a Mathlib LinearPMap on its exact operator range. The bounded Cauchy block viewed as a full-domain partial map is injective, has trivial kernel, the same range as the original continuous linear map, and a closed graph. Its LinearPMap inverse therefore has domain exactly the dense Cauchy range and is closed because its graph is the coordinate swap of the bounded graph. The inverse satisfies both exact inverse laws, is surjective onto the whole realified camera complexification, and is never represented as an everywhere-defined continuous linear map. This claim does not yet prove that the densely defined closed inverse is unbounded.
